guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul / Gibson ES-175 / Telecaster
guitar.evidence: Slash's Gibson Les Paul (famously a Kris Derrig replica used on Appetite for Destruction) is iconic; Izzy Stradlin's rhythm work on Telecaster/other guitars is also documented.

tone.target: dry Slash-style Marshall crunch with upper-mid bite
tone.profile: dry Slash-style Marshall crunch with upper-mid bite
tone.summary: A vintage British stack simulation using the UK 45 or UK 50 model, paired with a clean boost for definition, and limited modulation/delay to maintain riff tightness.
corrections: Name Marshall-family crunch, not generic rock tone.

rig.name: Guns N' Roses - Mr. Brownstone - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and background noise.
Provide the initial grit and upper-mid bite characteristic of Plexi crunch.
blocks.gap: The Blues OD is used to simulate a classic British overdrive stage, approximating the desired Marshall breakup without full saturation.

alternatives.reason: Similar character but might be too bright.

blocks.purpose: Used as a secondary crunch stage if the Blues OD is insufficient, but kept low to avoid excessive saturation.
blocks.gap: The RAT-style is generally too aggressive for this specific tone. It is included optionally and set very low (inactive) to maintain flexibility without compromising the core Plexi sound.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic Marshall Plexi tone (UK 50) with emphasis on upper-mids for bite.

alternatives.reason: Very close alternative, but UK 50 often captures the specific Plexi voicing better.

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic British cabinet voicing and punch.
Fine-tune the upper-mid bite and tighten the overall tone.
Kept inactive to ensure a dry, riff-forward sound.
blocks.gap: Modulation is generally avoided for this specific tight rock tone.

blocks.purpose: Add subtle definition and space without sounding lush or ambient.
blocks.gap: The delay is used minimally to add dimension, avoiding the 'lush ambience' that was requested to be avoided. Settings are kept low.

blocks.purpose: Provide a minimal sense of space (dry room feel) without excessive wash.
blocks.gap: The Room reverb is used sparingly to meet the 'dry roomless feel' requirement, keeping the decay time and mix low.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism to better capture the tight, upper-mid focused Marshall crunch.

proposals.reason: Enhance Plexi bite and tightness with a more authentic British cabinet sound.
proposals.whenToUse: After initial testing of the GP-180 preset chain
